Visit note | 2025-02-06 02:30 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Zakia Hossain, 51, female. Mrs. Hossain presents with a stiff shoulder for weeks, being unable to raise the arm, and being unable to reach behind the back. She states that her shoulder issues began after a minor fall at home in Badda. She works as an architect, which requires long hours at a drafting desk, and she lives with her family. She has Hypothyroidism. She denies any numbness or tingling down the arm, and her neck movements are full and painless. On examination, her shoulder lifts only to 100 degrees, active and passive ranges are restricted, and her other vitals are BP 121/70 mmHg, pulse 77 bpm, weight 75 kg. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. Advice provided: start physiotherapy, do pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up: 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Visit note | 2025-02-06 03:30 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Nurul Matubbar, 20, male. Mr. Matubbar reports spots on the back, pimples and blackheads on the face, and marks left after pimples. He notes that his condition has grown worse since working in a hot kitchen in Keraniganj. He works as a bus driver and lives in a shared mess. He has Essential hypertension. He denies any systemic symptoms like fever or joint pain. Examination reveals about 22 inflamed spots on the face, along with several comedones and post-inflammatory marks on his back, and other vitals show BP 144/88 mmHg, pulse 75 bpm, weight 57 kg. Assessment: Acne vulgaris. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to wash the face twice daily with a gentle cleanser and do not squeeze spots. Follow-up: 2 months.

Visit note | 2025-02-06 04:00 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Selim Pramanik, 44, male. Mr. Pramanik complains of being unable to raise the arm, being unable to reach behind the back, and night pain in the shoulder. He explains that his symptoms started after weeks of keeping the arm still after a sprain in Faridpur. He is a tailor by occupation, spending his days bent over a sewing machine, and lives with his spouse. He has no reported comorbidity. He has no neck tenderness or neurological deficits in the upper limb. On examination, shoulder lifts only to 65 degrees, with marked restriction in external rotation, while other vitals record BP 136/74 mmHg, pulse 86 bpm, weight 80 kg. Assessment: Adhesive capsulitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. Advice: start physiotherapy, do pendulum exercises daily, and apply heat before exercise. Follow-up: 4 weeks with a physiotherapy review.

Visit note | 2025-02-06 04:30 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Krishna Bose, 71, female. Mrs. Bose describes waking up tired and worry about sleep. She mentions that her sleep troubles began after starting rotating shifts at a factory in Kamrangirchar. She works as a farmer and lives with her extended family. She has Essential hypertension. She denies any depressed mood, daytime hallucinations, or substance use. On examination, her Insomnia Severity Index score is 18, and other vitals are BP 147/93 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, weight 79 kg. Assessment: Chronic insomnia. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to keep fixed sleep and wake times, avoid screens for an hour before bed, and avoid tea after 4 PM. Follow-up: 4 weeks with a sleep diary.

Visit note | 2025-02-08 09:00 AM | Dr. Farhana Kabir, General Medicine | Patient: Laila Mondal, 21, female. Ms. Mondal reports a fever that climbs a little higher every day for over a week and a coated tongue. She states that her illness began after a work trip to Chattogram where the water supply was unsafe. She works as a hotel receptionist and lives in Uttara. She has Bronchial asthma. She denies any dyspnoea, cough, or urinary symptoms. On examination, her temperature is 103.1°F, pulse is 99 bpm, and other vitals show BP 132/80 mmHg, weight 61 kg. Abdominal examination reveals mild splenomegaly. Assessment: Typhoid fever. Plan: a prescription was issued. Advice: eat soft home-cooked food, drink boiled or bottled water only, and avoid street food. Follow-up: 7 days with a repeat blood count.

Visit note | 2025-02-08 09:00 AM | Dr. Rumana Haque, Endocrinology | Patient: Dalia Gazi, 65, female. Mrs. Gazi complains of dry skin, feeling slow and tired, and always feeling cold. She notes these symptoms were found during tests for tiredness after moving to Gazipur. She is a retired civil servant and lives with her adult son. She has no other medical conditions. She denies chest pain, palpitations, or significant weight fluctuations. On examination, TSH is 12.7 mIU/L, and other vitals register BP 132/75 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 47 kg. Skin is dry and cool to the touch. Assessment: Hypothyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. Advice: keep a regular sleep routine and eat a balanced diet. Follow-up: 6 weeks with a repeat TSH.

Visit note | 2025-02-08 09:00 AM | Dr. Tahmina Begum, Dermatology | Patient: Jannat Chowdhury, 58, female. Mrs. Chowdhury attends for review regarding itchy raised welts that come and go and symptoms that started after a new food or medicine. She recalls it started after eating hilsa at a family dinner in Uttara. She works as a farmer and lives in a rural homestead. She has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies any breathing difficulty, lip swelling, or dizziness. Examination shows about 12 welts on the trunk and arms with surrounding erythema, and other vitals are BP 129/85 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, weight 61 kg. Assessment: Acute urticaria. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to avoid the suspected food, keep a symptom diary, and go to hospital at once if the tongue or throat swells. Follow-up: 2 weeks with the symptom diary.

Visit note | 2025-02-08 09:00 AM | Dr. Shamima Nasrin, Ophthalmology | Patient: Hasan Alam, 31, male. Mr. Alam presents with swelling of the eyelid and a painful red lump at the edge of the eyelid. He states it appeared after using old eye makeup in Badda. He works as a security guard and lives alone. He has no chronic illnesses. He denies any visual blurring or discharge from the other eye. On examination, there is a lump about 4 mm on the left upper eyelid with localized tenderness, and other vitals show BP 128/73 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, weight 52 kg. Note on presentation: a painless firm lump that has been present for weeks. Assessment: Hordeolum. Plan: a prescription was issued. Advice: use a warm compress four times a day, do not squeeze the lump, and avoid eye makeup. Follow-up: 1 week.

Visit note | 2025-02-08 09:00 AM | Dr. Ishrat Jahan, Psychiatry | Patient: Nayeem Ahmed, 39, male. Mr. Ahmed reports poor sleep, no interest in usual activities, and low energy. He notes that his symptoms began after losing a job in Bogura. He is a journalist by profession and lives with his parents. He has no physical comorbidities. The patient denies thoughts of self-harm, and a safety plan with the emergency number 999 was discussed. On examination, his PHQ-9 score is 15, and other vitals are BP 126/81 mmHg, pulse 68 bpm, weight 63 kg. Assessment: Depressive episode. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep a daily routine, walk outdoors daily, start counselling sessions, and call 999 or come to the clinic at once if thoughts of self-harm appear. Follow-up: 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-02-08 10:00 AM | Dr. Nusrat Jahan, General Medicine | Patient: Nusrat Gazi, 46, female. Mrs. Gazi complains of getting breathless on the stairs and constant tiredness. She states her fatigue worsened after a long spell of poor meals while living alone in Gulshan. She works as a bus driver and lives in a rental apartment. She has no underlying chronic conditions. She denies chest pain, dizziness, or gastrointestinal bleeding. On examination, her haemoglobin is 7.8 g/dL, pallor is noticeable, and other vitals record BP 129/75 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, weight 78 kg. Assessment: Iron deficiency anaemia. Plan: a prescription was issued. Advice: eat more lentils, spinach, liver, and eggs, and avoid tea within an hour of meals. Follow-up: 6 weeks with a repeat haemoglobin.

Visit note | 2025-02-08 10:00 AM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Mahfuz Rahman, 66, male. Mr. Rahman presents with a tight chest in dust or cold air and coughing at night. He mentions his symptoms flared during the winter smog in Uttara. He works as a homemaker and lives with his family. He has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. He denies fever, weight loss, or orthopnoea. On examination, SpO2 is 94% on room air, scattered expiratory wheezes are heard bilaterally, and other vitals show BP 112/79 mmHg, pulse 79 bpm, weight 83 kg. Assessment: Bronchial asthma. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid dust and smoke, keep the bedroom well aired, and learn the correct inhaler technique. Follow-up: 1 month to check inhaler technique.

Visit note | 2025-02-08 10:30 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Shirin Chowdhury, 66, female. Mrs. Chowdhury describes dizziness when looking up and brief spinning when turning in bed. She reports that her spells began after a viral cold in Kushtia. She works as a shopkeeper and lives with her children. She has Type 2 diabetes mellitus. She denies any tinnitus, hearing loss, or focal neurological weakness. On examination, the Dix-Hallpike test is positive on the left side with delayed-onset rotatory nystagmus, and other vitals are BP 127/81 mmHg, pulse 91 bpm, weight 58 kg. Assessment: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to get up slowly from bed, avoid sudden head movements, and repeat the Epley manoeuvre at home as shown. Follow-up: 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-02-08 10:30 AM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Laila Haque, 38, female. Mrs. Haque complains of itching and soreness. She states that her discomfort began during the humid monsoon in Rangpur. She works as a bus driver and lives in a family home. She has no chronic health issues. Assessment: Vulvovaginal candidiasis. Plan: a prescription was issued. Advice: wear cotton underwear, avoid scented soaps, and keep the area dry. Follow-up: 2 weeks if it does not clear.

Visit note | 2025-02-08 10:30 AM | Dr. Ishrat Jahan, Psychiatry | Patient: Rumana Howlader, 62, female. Mrs. Howlader reports feeling restless, poor sleep, and tense muscles. Visit note | 2025-02-09 11:30 AM | Dr. Moinul Haque, Neurology | Patient: Jahid Gazi, 75, male. Mr. Gazi describes persistent tingling like pins and needles and a burning sensation in both feet.
